author: Patrick Boyle
description:

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and with a budget estimated at one to one and a half billion dollars, it’s the most expensive video game ever made. In this video, Patrick Boyle looks at the economics behind the GTA 6 launch:

Why Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive could rationally bet so much on one game
How GTA 6 compares with megaprojects like the Burj Khalifa
Whether launch-day “lost productivity” forecasts hold up
How GTA Online and Shark Cards turned Rockstar into what is effectively a central bank, with inflation, capital controls, and a ban on rival currencies

We also look at who else is paying the bill, from UK video games tax relief to Miami’s GTA 6 marketing deal, and at what this blockbuster means for the future of the video game industry in the age of AI.
